extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for evaluating language agents' planning and tool-use capabilities in complex, real-world travel planning scenarios. It includes a sandbox environment with around four million data entries crawled from the internet, accessed via six tools (CitySearch, FlightSearch, DistanceMatrix, RestaurantSearch, AttractionSearch, AccommodationSearch). The dataset contains 1,225 meticulously curated planning intents and reference plans, each imposing different combinations of constraints (e.g., budget, room type, cuisine, transportation preferences). The benchmark evaluates agents' ability to satisfy user needs, commonsense constraints, and environment constraints while using tools to gather information.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su
extraction.publisher: Fudan University, The Ohio State University, The Pennsylvania State University, Meta AI
extraction.citeAs: TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed through a multi-step pipeline: 1) Environment and evaluation setup with a static sandbox containing around four million data entries crawled from the internet. 2) Diverse travel query design by randomly selecting departure cities, destinations, and date ranges, then adjusting duration and constraints to create varying complexity levels. 3) Reference plan annotation by 20 graduate students who meticulously created valid plans meeting all constraints, with each plan taking an average of 12 minutes to annotate. 4) Quality control through multiple stages of human verification, including re-calibration of budgets based on annotated plans to ensure feasibility.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of approximately four million entries crawled from the internet, including flight information, restaurant details, attraction listings, accommodation options, city data, and distance matrix information. Flight data was sourced from the Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset (spanning March 1 to April 1, 2022), restaurant data from the Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset, attraction data from Google Places API, and accommodation data from the Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset. The data was modified by adding, deleting, and altering keys/values to suit TravelPlanner's requirements and avoid contamination.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01 (flight data), with other data sources collected from publicly available internet sources
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The raw data was modified by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to suit TravelPlanner's requirements. Flight prices were generated by multiplying distance by a random factor (0.2 to 0.5). Accommodation data was assigned random room rules (e.g., 'No parties', 'No smoking', 'No children under 10', 'No pets', 'No visitors'). Restaurant data was categorized under different cuisines (Chinese, American, Italian, Mexican, Indian, Mediterranean, French).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data preprocessing involved: 1) Extracting relevant fields from source datasets (e.g., flight dates, times, distances, city names). 2) Generating derived fields like prices for flights and transportation. 3) Assigning categorical labels (cuisines, room types, room rules). 4) Randomly assigning entities to cities to create a realistic distribution. 5) Creating a static, closed sandbox environment to ensure consistent evaluations without dynamic data variability.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Reference plans were created by 20 graduate student annotators who meticulously designed plans meeting all constraints. Each plan was validated using pre-defined scripts that check for constraint satisfaction (e.g., budget limits, room type preferences, commonsense constraints). Annotators were paid an average of $0.80 per plan. The authors performed detailed reviews of every query and plan to ensure quality and rectify errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Manual annotation by human annotators using standard text editors and validation scripts
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process ensured that each query had at least one feasible plan by requiring annotators to create plans that met all constraints. The validation scripts automatically checked for constraint satisfaction across multiple dimensions (commonsense constraints, hard constraints, environment constraints). The process resulted in 1,225 validated query-plan pairs with high quality assurance through multiple stages of human verification.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 graduate students participated in the annotation process, with an average of $0.80 payment per plan annotated. The authors performed quality control reviews of all annotations.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark provides evaluation scripts to foster innovation and aid development of new methods. The authors encourage using evaluation feedback in training sets (e.g., reinforcement learning techniques) but prohibit cheating in validation and test sets to maintain fairness. The dataset is designed to be a challenging yet meaningful testbed for future research.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to advance research in complex planning capabilities for language agents, potentially contributing to more capable AI systems that could automate tedious real-world planning tasks. The authors note that while current agents struggle significantly, the mere possibility of tackling such complex problems represents non-trivial progress toward human-level planning capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases inherent in the source data (e.g., geographic distribution of restaurants, attractions, and accommodations from public internet sources). The evaluation criteria are based on the authors' consensus of commonsense constraints, which may differ from other perspectives. The authors acknowledge that everyone's definition of commonsense may vary and encourage additional discussions to enrich the commonsense dimensions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: 1) Current language agents perform poorly on complex multi-constraint tasks (GPT-4 achieves only 0.6% success rate). 2) Agents struggle with tool-use errors, dead loops, and hallucinations. 3) Performance deteriorates when multitasking (information collection + planning). 4) Agents fail to consider multiple constraints holistically. 5) The benchmark focuses on travel planning, which may not generalize to other domains. 6) The static sandbox environment may not capture real-world dynamism. Non-recommended uses include relying on current agents for critical planning decisions without human oversight.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-tuning for language agents' planning and tool-use capabilities. The benchmark is designed to evaluate agents' ability to: 1) Use tools to gather information from a partially observable environment. 2) Satisfy multiple constraints (budget, room type, cuisine, transportation preferences). 3) Incorporate commonsense constraints (e.g., reasonable city routes, diverse restaurants/attractions). 4) Handle environment constraints (e.g., unavailable transportation or attractions). The authors encourage using evaluation feedback in training sets to improve methods while maintaining fairness in validation and test sets.
